producer: Write a scoped game design brief, creative direction, milestone plan, and acceptance criteria.
gameplay: Implement the mechanic in the project engine. Add focused tests or a reproducible scenario. Preserve existing behavior.
world: Design the level, lighting, camera, navigation, and VFX. Document profiling targets and scene edits.
models: Find licensed assets or create models in Blender. Deliver editable source, FBX for Unity or GLB for Godot, previews, metrics, and provenance. Check scale, pivot, materials, collision, and rig compatibility.
ui: Design an accessible HUD and menus. Use Photoshop for layered masters when available. Deliver PNG derivatives, focus order, interaction states, and layout notes.
audio: Design a cue map and mixer groups. Source or produce licensed effects, ambience, and music. Deliver WAV masters and playback notes, including looping and gain.
integrator: Own the final project changes. Validate and import approved derivatives, preserve engine asset references, wire UI and audio, and build the playable revision.
qa: Run independently reproducible gameplay checks against the built game. Test win, restart, controls, accessibility, audio, visuals, and budget. Provide a verdict with observed evidence.
marketing: Draft positioning, store copy, trailer shot list, layered key art and store/social variants where possible. Use build-linked captures, truthful claims, and provenance. Stage materials for creator review.
